name: ICELAND

flag.title: Flag of Iceland
flag.note: Blue with a red cross edged in white

lead: Iceland sits near the Arctic. Volcanoes rumble under its glaciers. On winter nights, the sky glows green. Fewer than 400,000 people live here. Volcano heat gives them free hot water and heating.

facts.label: Area
facts.sub: About the size of Kentucky, USA

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Two tectonic plates (giant rock slabs) pull apart under Iceland, 2 cm a year. Iceland has over 130 volcanoes. About 30 are still active.
More than 10% of Iceland is glacier, yet the ground underneath is warm. The geyser Strokkur shoots boiling water 20 metres high every few minutes.
animals: Iceland has no bears, wolves, or snakes. The Arctic fox is the only land mammal that came on its own. It crossed frozen sea ice thousands of years ago.
Humpback whales and orcas swim offshore. Millions of puffins nest here each summer. Their stubby wings beat up to 400 times a minute.
culture: Icelanders love 'hot pots', outdoor pools heated by the Earth. Every town has one. Soaking at 40 °C while snowflakes land on your head is a normal Tuesday.
Iceland reads more books per person than almost anywhere. On Christmas Eve, everyone gives novels to read in bed. This is the 'Jólabókaflóð', or Christmas Book Flood.
history: Vikings from Norway settled Iceland around 874 AD. In 930 AD, Icelanders created the Althing, one of the world's oldest parliaments. People debated laws in the open air.

Denmark ruled for centuries. In 1783, eruptions killed a quarter of Icelanders. Independence came in 1944. In one generation, Iceland went from one of Europe's poorest countries to one of its wealthiest.
wows: Nearly 100% of Iceland's electricity comes from underground heat or flowing water.
The Northern Lights dance green and purple over Reykjavik on clear winter nights.
Icelanders have no family surnames, only a parent's first name plus -son or -dóttir.
Iceland has no army, navy, or air force.
At Silfra, a crack between two tectonic plates, you can swim and see 100 m ahead.
Roads bend around rocks where the hidden folk (Huldufólk) are said to live.
Eyjafjallajökull erupted in 2010 and grounded millions of airline passengers.

myths.myth: The Northern Lights shine all year
myths.fact: Summer nights are too bright to see them. They show best from about September to April.
No horned Viking helmet has ever been found. The idea came from costumes in 1800s operas.
